Timeline::span¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Series Timeline::span(
    const Timeline& other,
    const TimelineSpanOptions& options = {}) const

Measure From This Timeline To Another¶

span() counts temporal units from the receiver to other. The receiver is the start and other is the end. It returns signed 64-bit integer counts in a Series, preserving the broadcasted shape of the two temporal operands.

This method exists because “distance in time” has several valid meanings:

  • elapsed nanoseconds, seconds, hours, or exact 24-hour days

  • completed calendar months or years

  • crossed month or year labels

  • working dates selected by a weekday and holiday calendar

Those meanings cannot be inferred from one integer argument. TimelineSpanOptions makes the choice explicit and keeps unit counting separate from diff(), which always returns the exact elapsed distance as a Duration.

The default options count complete elapsed 24-hour days and preserve direction. Each field has a deliberately narrow role:

Field

Meaning

Default

Applies to

unit

Selects the elapsed, calendar, or business unit to count.

TimelineSpanUnit::Days

Every call

mode

Chooses completed units or crossed calendar labels.

TimelineSpanMode::Complete

Months, Years

anchor

Decides whether month ends correspond when a strict day number does not exist.

TimelineSpanAnchor::DayOfMonth

Complete Months, complete Years

signed_result

Preserves direction when true; returns the non-negative magnitude when false.

true

Every unit

calendar

Supplies the working-week mask, holiday dates, and optional timezone constraint.

Monday-Friday, no holidays, no timezone constraint

BusinessDays

closed

Selects which endpoint dates are eligible for business-day counting.

TimelineSpanClosed::Right

BusinessDays

Fields outside the selected unit’s “Applies to” column are ignored. In particular, changing mode, anchor, calendar, or closed cannot alter a fixed elapsed-unit result.

Fixed Elapsed Units¶

The fixed units are:

Unit

Exact divisor

Nanos

1 ns

Micros

1,000 ns

Millis

1,000,000 ns

Seconds

1,000,000,000 ns

Minutes

60 seconds

Hours

3,600 seconds

Days

86,400 seconds

Weeks

604,800 seconds

For these units, span() subtracts epoch instants and divides by the selected unit. An incomplete unit is discarded by integer truncation toward zero. It does not round to the nearest unit.

Example 1. Default options count one complete elapsed day in a distance of one day, one hour, two minutes, three seconds, and 210 nanoseconds.

const auto start =
    pluss::timeline::make("2024-01-01T00:00:00.123456789Z");
const auto end =
    pluss::timeline::make("2024-01-02T01:02:03.123456999Z");
std::cout << pluss::series::print(start.span(end)) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=1

Example 2. Select a fixed unit by changing only unit. Each result is an integer count from the same exact difference.

auto options = pluss::TimelineSpanOptions{};

options.unit = pluss::TimelineSpanUnit::Nanos;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(start.span(end, options)) << '\n';
options.unit = pluss::TimelineSpanUnit::Micros;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(start.span(end, options)) << '\n';
options.unit = pluss::TimelineSpanUnit::Millis;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(start.span(end, options)) << '\n';
options.unit = pluss::TimelineSpanUnit::Seconds;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(start.span(end, options)) << '\n';
options.unit = pluss::TimelineSpanUnit::Minutes;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(start.span(end, options)) << '\n';
options.unit = pluss::TimelineSpanUnit::Hours;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(start.span(end, options)) << '\n';
options.unit = pluss::TimelineSpanUnit::Weeks;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(start.span(end, options)) << '\n';

Elapsed Days Are Not Civil Days¶

TimelineSpanUnit::Days means an exact 86,400-second divisor. It does not count date labels. A pair of equal local clock readings on consecutive dates can be 23 or 25 elapsed hours apart when the UTC offset changes.

Example 3. The next civil day across this spring transition is 23 elapsed hours away. It therefore contains zero complete elapsed Days.

const auto spring = pluss::timeline::make("2024-03-09T10:30:00Z")
                        .tz_convert("America/Edmonton");
const auto next_civil_day = spring.add_days(1);
auto options = pluss::TimelineSpanOptions{};
options.unit = pluss::TimelineSpanUnit::Hours;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(spring.span(next_civil_day, options)) << '\n';
std::cout << pluss::series::print(spring.span(next_civil_day)) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=23
Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=0

Direction And Absolute Magnitude¶

With the default signed_result=true, reversing the operands reverses the sign. Set signed_result=false when direction is irrelevant and only the non-negative magnitude is wanted. Absolute conversion happens before range validation, without relying on negating the most-negative 64-bit value.

Example 4. The same reverse span can be signed or absolute.

auto options = pluss::TimelineSpanOptions{};
options.unit = pluss::TimelineSpanUnit::Seconds;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(end.span(start, options)) << '\n';

options.signed_result = false;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(end.span(start, options)) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=-90123
Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=90123

Broadcasting And Output Shape¶

The two timelines follow trailing-axis broadcasting. A scalar pairs with every element of an array; equal shapes pair elementwise; singleton dimensions can expand. Incompatible dimensions are rejected. The output is a new contiguous int64 Series with the broadcasted shape.

Example 5. A scalar start is measured against two end instants. The second distance is two complete days because the extra twelve hours are truncated.

const auto scalar = pluss::timeline::make("2024-01-01T00:00:00Z");
const auto vector = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2024-01-02T00:00:00Z",
    "2024-01-03T12:00:00Z",
});
std::cout << pluss::series::print(scalar.span(vector)) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 2]

Example 6. Broadcasting can expand both operands. Shapes [2, 1] and [1, 2] produce a [2, 2] matrix of pairwise day counts.

const std::vector<std::string> column_values{
    "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", "2024-01-02T00:00:00Z"};
const std::vector<std::string> row_values{
    "2024-01-03T00:00:00Z", "2024-01-05T00:00:00Z"};
const auto column = pluss::timeline::make(column_values, {2, 1});
const auto row = pluss::timeline::make(row_values, {1, 2});
std::cout << pluss::series::print(column.span(row)) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ 2 4 ⎤
⎣ 1 3 ⎦

Completed Calendar Months¶

TimelineSpanUnit::Months uses local calendar fields rather than a fixed duration. With mode=Complete, a month is counted only after the destination has reached the required local day and time of day.

The default anchor=DayOfMonth is strict: January 31 to February 29 is not a complete month because the destination never reaches day 31. Set anchor=MonthEnd when the final valid day of each month should be treated as the corresponding monthly position.

Month-end equivalence does not discard clock precision. If the destination is one nanosecond before the source clock, the month is still incomplete.

Example 7. The three complete-month outcomes isolate day anchoring and the time-of-day boundary.

const auto jan31_noon = pluss::timeline::make("2024-01-31T12:00:00Z");
const auto feb29_early =
    pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-29T11:59:59.999999999Z");
const auto feb29_noon = pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-29T12:00:00Z");

auto options = pluss::TimelineSpanOptions{};
options.unit = pluss::TimelineSpanUnit::Months;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(jan31_noon.span(feb29_noon, options)) << '\n';

options.anchor = pluss::TimelineSpanAnchor::MonthEnd;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(jan31_noon.span(feb29_early, options)) << '\n';
std::cout << pluss::series::print(jan31_noon.span(feb29_noon, options)) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=0
Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=0
Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=1

Calendar Boundaries Instead Of Complete Units¶

mode=Boundary counts changes in the calendar label. For months, it computes the difference between year/month labels; for years, it computes the difference between year labels. The day and time do not need to reach an anniversary. anchor has no effect in boundary mode.

Example 8. January to February crosses one month boundary even though the end is one nanosecond short of the month-end clock anchor.

auto options = pluss::TimelineSpanOptions{};
options.unit = pluss::TimelineSpanUnit::Months;
options.mode = pluss::TimelineSpanMode::Boundary;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(jan31_noon.span(feb29_early, options)) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=1

Completed Calendar Years¶

TimelineSpanUnit::Years follows the same policies at annual scale. Complete mode requires the local anniversary date and clock. MonthEnd anchoring treats the final day of February in a non-leap year as corresponding to leap day; strict DayOfMonth anchoring does not.

Example 9. The anchor determines whether this leap-day interval contains one complete calendar year.

const auto leap = pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-29T12:00:00Z");
const auto next_feb_end = pluss::timeline::make("2025-02-28T12:00:00Z");
auto options = pluss::TimelineSpanOptions{};
options.unit = pluss::TimelineSpanUnit::Years;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(leap.span(next_feb_end, options)) << '\n';

options.anchor = pluss::TimelineSpanAnchor::MonthEnd;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(leap.span(next_feb_end, options)) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=0
Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=1

Business-Day Counting¶

Select BusinessDays to count local calendar dates admitted by a BusinessCalendar. A calendar contains:

  • a seven-bit weekmask, using Sunday as bit 0 through Saturday as bit 6

  • local epoch-day holiday labels to exclude

  • descriptive name and region metadata

  • an optional required timezone

BusinessCalendar::monfri() admits Monday through Friday and has no holidays. Built-in constructors provide usa_federal, canada_federal, uk_bank, target2, and nyse holiday sets for an inclusive year range. Choose a range that covers every endpoint you will measure; dates outside that generated range still follow the weekmask but have no generated holiday exclusions.

The closed option determines which endpoint dates can be counted:

Value

Interval

Right

(start, end]

Left

[start, end)

Both

[start, end]

Neither

(start, end)

Closure applies to local dates, not clock instants. Weekend and holiday dates remain excluded even when closed. mode and anchor do not alter business-day counting.

Example 10. From Friday to Monday, each closure policy selects a different combination of endpoint dates. Weekend dates remain excluded in every case.

const auto friday = pluss::timeline::make("2024-07-05T15:00:00Z");
const auto monday = pluss::timeline::make("2024-07-08T09:00:00Z");
auto options = pluss::TimelineSpanOptions{};
options.unit = pluss::TimelineSpanUnit::BusinessDays;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(friday.span(monday, options)) << '\n';

options.closed = pluss::TimelineSpanClosed::Both;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(friday.span(monday, options)) << '\n';
options.closed = pluss::TimelineSpanClosed::Left;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(friday.span(monday, options)) << '\n';
options.closed = pluss::TimelineSpanClosed::Neither;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(friday.span(monday, options)) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=1
Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=2
Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=1
Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=0

Example 11. A custom holiday is supplied as a local epoch-day label. Marking the Monday endpoint as a holiday reduces the right-closed result to zero.

auto options = pluss::TimelineSpanOptions{};
options.unit = pluss::TimelineSpanUnit::BusinessDays;
options.calendar.holidays =
    pluss::timeline::date("2024-07-08")
        .epoch_days()
        .to_vec<std::int64_t>();
std::cout << pluss::series::print(friday.span(monday, options)) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=0

Example 12. A custom weekmask can define a different working week. This mask admits Saturday only, so the open-start, closed-end interval from Friday to Monday counts the intervening Saturday.

auto options = pluss::TimelineSpanOptions{};
options.unit = pluss::TimelineSpanUnit::BusinessDays;
options.calendar.weekmask = 0b1000000;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(friday.span(monday, options)) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=1

Example 13. A generated federal calendar excludes the Monday holiday, while a plain weekday calendar counts both Monday and Tuesday.

const auto before = pluss::timeline::make("2024-06-28T12:00:00Z");
const auto after = pluss::timeline::make("2024-07-02T12:00:00Z");
auto options = pluss::TimelineSpanOptions{};
options.unit = pluss::TimelineSpanUnit::BusinessDays;
options.calendar = pluss::BusinessCalendar::canada_federal(2024, 2024);
std::cout << pluss::series::print(before.span(after, options)) << '\n';

options.calendar = pluss::BusinessCalendar::monfri();
std::cout << pluss::series::print(before.span(after, options)) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=1
Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=2

Timezone Rules¶

Fixed elapsed units compare stored instants, so the two timelines may carry different timezone labels. Months, years, and business days read local dates; they require matching timezone names to prevent an implicit choice of calendar. A business calendar with a non-empty timezone must also match the timeline. Convert explicitly with tz_convert() before measuring when calendar labels must be interpreted in a chosen zone.

Example 14. A calendar span with unlike timezone labels is rejected even when both values identify the same instant.

try {
  const auto utc = pluss::timeline::make("2024-01-01T00:00:00Z");
  const auto local = utc.tz_convert("America/Edmonton");
  auto options = pluss::TimelineSpanOptions{};
  options.unit = pluss::TimelineSpanUnit::Months;
  (void)utc.span(local, options);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "rejected\n";
}

Output¶

rejected

Absent Instants, Empty Shapes, And Strides¶

If either paired instant is NaT, the corresponding integer result is Timeline::kNaT. This sentinel is the minimum signed 64-bit value and prints as -9223372036854775808 in the returned numeric Series. Other pairs are still measured normally.

Empty broadcast-compatible shapes return an empty Series with the broadcasted shape. Non-contiguous timeline inputs are read by logical strides rather than as packed storage.

Example 15. Absence propagates elementwise.

const auto values = pluss::timeline::make({"2024-01-01", ""});
std::cout << pluss::series::print(
    values.span(pluss::timeline::date("2024-01-03"))) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[2, -9223372036854775808]

Example 16. A zero-length leading dimension remains part of the result shape.

const auto empty = pluss::timeline::epoch({0, 2});
std::cout << pluss::series::print(
    empty.span(pluss::timeline::from_epoch(0LL))) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[0,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=0, contiguous=true)
[]

Validation And Range Safety¶

span() rejects:

  • non-broadcastable timeline shapes

  • calendar or business spans with different timezone names

  • an empty business weekmask or bits outside the seven weekdays

  • a timezone-constrained business calendar used with another timezone

  • holiday entries that are Timeline::kNaT or look like epoch nanoseconds

  • a final count that cannot fit in signed int64

Subtraction is widened before division. This matters near the epoch-storage limits: a seconds quotient can fit even when the raw nanosecond difference does not. A nanosecond count for that same pair is rejected instead of wrapping.

Example 17. The full-range seconds quotient is representable, but the nanosecond count is not.

const auto near_min = pluss::timeline::from_epoch(
    std::numeric_limits<std::int64_t>::min() + 1);
const auto near_max = pluss::timeline::from_epoch(
    std::numeric_limits<std::int64_t>::max());
auto options = pluss::TimelineSpanOptions{};
options.unit = pluss::TimelineSpanUnit::Seconds;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(near_min.span(near_max, options)) << '\n';

try {
  options.unit = pluss::TimelineSpanUnit::Nanos;
  (void)near_min.span(near_max, options);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "rejected\n";
}

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=18446744073
rejected

Choosing The Right Measurement¶

Use span() when the result must be an integer count under an explicit unit or calendar policy. Use diff() when you need the exact elapsed Duration, want duration arithmetic afterward, or do not want truncation. Use the add_* family when the task is to construct shifted timestamps rather than measure existing pairs.

See Also¶

  • Timeline::diff: exact elapsed distance as a Duration.

  • Timeline::add_days: move by civil days rather than measure elapsed days.

  • Timeline::tz_convert: choose the calendar timezone explicitly.
